subject: Pegasus renewal — surge safety, price hold & commit options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rossi <marta@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.p@pegasus.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift options

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Attached is the renewal proposal for Pegasus (term starting 2027-01-01) that reflects the baseline 12-month renewal at your current commit plus two optional uplift tranches we discussed: +30% burst pool for seasonal campaigns and a staged capacity uplift to support a new pilot.

TL;DR of the commercial:
- Base commit: 2M tokens/month at current unit rate (no change)
- Uplift tranche A: +30% burst pool (pre-paid credit) — one-time credit applied to Q1
- Uplift tranche B: phased capacity increase (months 4–12) with a 10% conditional discount if usage reaches 85% of committed capacity
- One-year term; standard enterprise SLA

Attachment: Pegasus_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Can you confirm whether you want both uplift tranches priced in the master, or whether we should leave the uplift as an on-demand add-on and just lock the base commit/price?

Happy to set a call to walk the options.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0193
From: Marta Rossi <marta@pegasus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift options

Jordan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear options. A couple of asks from procurement and engineering before we move forward: 
1) Price hold: can you hold the base unit price for 18 months (covering our fiscal year) if we sign the 12-month renewal today?
2) Surge safety: we need a predictable surge path for campaign spikes without punitive overage rates. Prefer a pre-agreed burst credit bucket or a capped overage rate.
3) Legal wants the uplift tranche language simplified — they prefer to see a deterministic trigger (e.g., sustained 85% usage for 30 days) rather than vague operational language.

If you can get back with a counter that includes a price hold commitment, a clear burst-credit mechanism, and simpler trigger language, we should be ready to move to PO/DocuSign.

Regards,
Marta Rossi
Head of Procurement, Pegasus AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pegasus asks — price hold, surge safety, trigger language (need quick pricing/legal take)

Team —

Fwd'ing Pegasus's asks. They want: an 18‑month price hold on the base unit, a pre‑agreed burst credit bucket in lieu of harsh overage, and tightened trigger language for the phased uplift. They indicated readiness to PO if we can accommodate.

Options I'm thinking (please weigh in):
A) Price hold: 18 months on base unit in exchange for a modest up-front credit (5% of annual committed spend).
B) Surge safety: 30% burst pool as pre-paid credit applied against overage; unused credits roll to Q2 only, no further roll-forward.
C) Trigger: phased uplift unlocks after sustained 85% commit utilization for any rolling 21-day window (to be conservative).

Questions: can legal accept 21 days instead of 30? Finance: will 5% up-front credit cover expected margin impact? Ops: can autoscaling and capacity reservations be honored with the above?

I'd like to respond with a formal counter by COB Monday.

-Jordan
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pegasus asks — recommendation for counteroffer

Jordan / Karthik —

Quick take from pricing & finance: we can do the price hold and burst-credit approach with these constraints: 
- Price hold: grant an 18-month price protection on the base unit if Pegasus agrees to a 6% prepayment credit (applied up front against the first invoice). This recoups risk and keeps net present value neutral.
- Burst credit: offer a 25% burst pool (smaller than their ask) as pre-paid credits; unused credits expire at end of Q2. This balances operational risk and revenue predictability.
- Trigger language: legal — Laura, can you sign off on 21-day rolling 85% trigger? If not, suggest 30 days but include a one-time discretionary waive in quarter 1 if engineering flags a false positive.

If legal signs off on 21 days, we should present the counter as: 18‑month price hold (6% prepay), 25% pre-paid burst pool, uplift tranche lock at 85% sustained utilization over 21 days. I'll draft the commercial redline.

-Vanessa
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Rossi <marta@pegasus.ai>, Arjun Patel <arjun.p@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal and capacity uplift options — formal counter

Marta / Arjun —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per internal alignment, please find our formal counter (summary below) and the attached commercial redline. Key points: 
- Price protection: 18-month hold on the base unit price if Pegasus signs the 12-month renewal on or before 2026-11-20. This is conditional on a 6% prepayment credit applied to the first invoice.
- Surge safety: 25% pre-paid burst credit bucket (one-time credit applied to spike usage). Unused credits expire 2027-06-30.
- Phased uplift trigger: uplift tranche unlocks after sustained 85% commit utilization for any rolling 21-day window (system metrics to be the source of truth).
- Term and SLA otherwise as proposed.

Attachment: Pegasus_Renewal_Counter_20261116.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

If this aligns, we'll prepare an amendment and a DocuSign envelope. We can also convert the 6% prepay into monthly amortization if you prefer (we can offer the accounting flex).

Best,
Jordan
